data.label: evaluation numeric value
data.scopeNote: Present only when the source printed a number, or when the value is explicitly marked as an analyst-defined decision-model value via mdcore:valueProvenance.

data.definition: Relates a behavior to a structure or design alternative whose configuration makes that behavior possible.
data.label: enabled by

data.definition: A condition that must hold for the behavior to occur at all, for example a maintained normal pressure for a friction-based load transfer.
data.label: behavior requires condition
has advantage
data.scopeNote: Points at an evaluation so that the advantage carries its context and provenance, rather than being a bare string.

data.definition: Two alternatives can perform at least one common function. Symmetric, because co-function genuinely is symmetric -- unlike substitutability, which is not.
data.label: shares function with

data.definition: A convenience shortcut from candidate to baseline, materialised by the build pipeline from an existing SubstitutionAssessment and never asserted by hand.
data.label: substitution assessed as
data.scopeNote: Explicitly NOT owl:SymmetricProperty and NOT owl:TransitiveProperty. Any reasoner configuration that makes it either is a misuse of this ontology.

data.label: may experience failure mode
data.scopeNote: Modal by design: asserts possibility in some context, not inevitability. Pair with mdcore:aggravatedByCondition to say when.

data.definition: Relates a design alternative to a function it is capable of delivering. This is the entry point for the query 'what can perform this function?'.
data.label: performs function
data.scopeNote: Shared performsFunction is necessary but NOT sufficient for substitutability. See mdcore:SubstitutionAssessment.

data.definition: Relates an artifact to an artifact contained within it.
data.label: has part

data.definition: Relates an artifact to a function it is intended to deliver. Intent, not observed behaviour.
data.label: has function

data.definition: The geometry feature at which the failure characteristically starts, such as a keyseat or a fillet.
data.label: initiates at geometry feature

data.definition: Relates a function to a behavior that produces it.
data.label: realized by

data.definition: Relates an interface to each artifact it joins.
data.label: connects

data.definition: A quantified parameter of the condition, with its unit.
data.label: condition parameter

data.definition: The alternative currently assumed, which the candidate would displace.
data.label: baseline alternative

data.definition: The alternative proposed as a replacement.
data.label: candidate alternative
function being preserved
data.scopeNote: Mandatory. Substitution claims that do not say what is being preserved are not interpretable.

data.definition: A condition that must hold for the conclusion to apply.
data.label: substitution condition

meta.description: General engineering-design concepts and the evidence model. Nothing here mentions a shaft, a key or a bearing — that is the test of whether the core is genuinely reusable.
notes: Solid edges are rdfs:subClassOf. Dashed edges are object properties, drawn from declared domain to declared range; select one to see its definition.
Every class here is ontology engineering, not source-derived content.
meta.title: Core ontology (Level 1)

data.definition: A work, independent of any particular edition or printing.
data.label: Book

data.definition: A specific edition of a book. Claims are attached to editions, never to works, because pagination, equation numbering and content differ between editions.
data.label: Book Edition

data.definition: A normalized claim proposed for promotion into the rule layer, not yet accepted.
data.label: Candidate Design Rule

data.definition: A single assertion attributed to a source, held as data rather than as an ontology axiom, so that it can be conditioned, contradicted, revised or rejected without touching the schema.
data.label: Claim
data.scopeNote: Claims are ABox individuals. Promotion of a claim into a TBox axiom or an executable rule is a separate, human-authorised step.

data.definition: A reified comparison of two claims from different sources, recording how they relate without merging them.
data.label: Claim Alignment
data.scopeNote: Conflicting claims are preserved side by side. Reconciliation is never silent.

data.definition: A mapping between a source-specific term or symbol and a core-ontology concept, or between the corresponding terms of two sources.
data.label: Concept Alignment

data.definition: An ordered procedure printed in a source, cited as a unit because its steps are only valid together.
data.label: Design Procedure

data.definition: Anything that supports or contradicts a claim.
data.label: Evidence

data.definition: A located, quotable region of a source document: a document, a page, a block, optionally a bounding box, and the text that was actually extracted from it.
data.label: Evidence Span
data.scopeNote: Excerpts are kept short. The purpose of the stored text is to make the citation verifiable by re-reading the page, not to reproduce the book.

data.definition: A claim as first obtained from the source text, before normalisation.
data.label: Extracted Claim

data.definition: A manufacturer's published data source, cited but not reproduced.
data.label: Manufacturer Catalog

data.definition: A claim restated in controlled vocabulary, with conditions and units made explicit.
data.label: Normalized Claim

data.definition: One page of one source document, carrying both its zero-based PDF index and its printed label.
data.label: Page

data.definition: The concrete file that was processed, identified by file name and SHA-256, so that provenance cannot silently drift onto a different scan of the same edition.
data.label: Source Document

data.definition: A published standard referenced by a source. Referencing a standard is not the same as reproducing it: the ontology records that a standard governs a value, not the value itself, unless the source printed it.
data.label: Standard

data.definition: A concept alignment concerned specifically with vocabulary or symbol usage.
data.label: Terminology Alignment

data.definition: A symbol appearing in an equation, together with its meaning, dimension and preferred unit, scoped to the source that used it.
data.label: Variable

outgoing.label: local definition as given by the source

data.scopeNote: Variables are source-scoped on purpose. Mott's k and Shigley's a are the same physical exponent but are NOT merged; they are linked through a ConceptAlignment instead.

data.definition: Declared outside the core modules; shown so that its subclasses are not stranded.
data.label: //www.w3.org/2004/02/skos/core#Concept

data.definition: The condition a verification result must meet for the design to be judged acceptable.
data.label: Acceptance Criterion

data.definition: A reified statement that a design alternative attains a stated level on a stated criterion, in a stated context, on stated authority.
data.label: Alternative Evaluation
data.scopeNote: Reified because the same alternative scores differently on the same criterion in different contexts, and because the provenance of each score must travel with it.

data.definition: A derived model of behaviour, stated with its assumptions and validity conditions.
data.label: Analytical Model

data.definition: A designed artifact produced by joining two or more artifacts through interfaces, and which is handled as a single item at the next level of assembly.
data.label: Assembly

data.definition: Constraint arising from procurement lead time or from whether an element is a standard, catalogue item.
data.label: Availability Constraint

data.definition: A physical process by which a structure produces a function under given operating conditions, described in terms of the quantities that are exchanged or transformed.
data.label: Behavior
data.scopeNote: Behavior answers 'by what mechanism?'. 'Transmit torque' is a Function; 'transfer load by shear across a shaft/hub interface' is a Behavior.

data.comment: Reified so that the reason an alternative was excluded from consideration is recoverable, not lost.
data.definition: The set of design alternatives admitted to comparison for a given design problem, together with the filter that produced it.
data.label: Candidate Set

data.definition: Two or more load types acting together, e.g. bending with torsion.
data.label: Combined Loading

data.definition: A designed artifact treated as atomic at the level of decomposition currently under consideration. Atomicity is relative to the analysis, not absolute: a rolling bearing is a component to a shaft designer and an assembly to a bearing manufacturer.
data.label: Component

data.definition: A requirement that bounds the admissible solution space rather than expressing a desired level of performance; it is satisfied or violated, and is not traded off.
data.label: Constraint
data.scopeNote: Distinguishing Constraint from the general Requirement matters for decision-making: constraints filter the candidate set before any weighting or scoring is applied.

data.definition: Load that varies repeatedly with time, so that fatigue is a candidate failure mechanism.
data.label: Cyclic Loading

data.definition: The stated reasoning for a design decision, including the criteria that dominated and the alternatives rejected.
data.label: Decision Rationale

data.definition: A candidate solution concept that could be adopted to satisfy a design problem: a class of artifact, a working principle, or a specific configuration.
data.label: Design Alternative
data.scopeNote: A DesignAlternative is a *solution concept*, not an individual manufactured item. 'Parallel key connection' is an alternative; 'the key in gearbox serial 4471' is not.

data.definition: A recorded commitment to one alternative for a design problem, with the evaluations and rationale that supported it.
data.label: Design Decision

data.comment: Broader than GeometryFeature: a surface treatment or a specified fit is a DesignFeature but not a GeometryFeature.
data.definition: Any deliberate characteristic of an artifact -- geometric, material, dimensional or procedural -- introduced to influence behaviour, for example to mitigate a failure mode.
data.label: Design Feature

data.definition: A change to geometry, material, tolerance, interface or process that must be carried out before a candidate can take the baseline's place.
data.label: Design Modification

data.definition: A stated need for a design solution, characterised by the functions required, the operating context, and the requirements and constraints that a solution must satisfy.
data.label: Design Problem

data.definition: A conditional statement of the form 'in context C, for requirement set R, do or prefer X', held as a citable object with its own provenance and review state.
data.label: Design Rule
data.scopeNote: Every DesignRule must either name an applicable context or declare mdcore:contextUnspecified true. A rule with neither is invalid.

data.definition: Any human-made entity that is the intended outcome of a design process, and about which functions, requirements and design decisions can be asserted. Deliberately domain-neutral: a designed artifact may be mechanical, electrical, software or organisational.
data.label: Designed Artifact
data.scopeNote: Use for the thing being designed, not for the design description of it. A drawing of a shaft is a document, not a DesignedArtifact.

data.definition: A closed-form design calculation, typically a sizing or stress check.
data.label: Engineering Calculation

data.definition: A dimension along which design alternatives are compared, derived from a requirement or from a stakeholder concern.
data.label: Evaluation Criterion

data.definition: The kind of external source that must supply what the textbooks left unspecified.
data.label: External Authority Kind

data.definition: The effect of a failure mode on the containing system, including whether the failure is benign, protective, or damaging to adjacent components.
data.label: Failure Consequence
data.scopeNote: Needed to represent deliberately sacrificial elements, where failure of one part is the intended way to protect others.

data.definition: The physical, chemical or tribological process by which a failure mode develops: fatigue crack growth, plastic yielding, adhesive wear, corrosion, creep, fretting.
data.label: Failure Mechanism

data.definition: The manner in which an artifact ceases to perform a required function, described observably: fracture, excessive deflection, loss of clamping, surface pitting, loosening.
data.label: Failure Mode

data.definition: An intended, solution-neutral effect that a designed artifact is required to produce, expressed as a transformation of energy, material, motion, force or information.
data.label: Function
data.scopeNote: Name functions as verb phrases ('transmit torque from shaft to hub'), never as element names ('key'). A function that can only be stated by naming one solution is not solution-neutral and is probably a Requirement or a DesignAlternative in disguise.

data.comment: Reified so that competing decompositions of the same function can coexist and be compared, rather than being merged.
data.definition: A reified statement that one function is fulfilled by a named set of sub-functions under a stated rationale.
data.label: Function Decomposition

data.definition: A named, bounded portion of an artifact's shape that carries design intent, for example a groove, a fillet, a shoulder or a hole. Geometry features are the usual carriers of stress concentration and of manufacturing and inspection requirements.
data.label: Geometry Feature

data.definition: A region, surface or logical boundary at which two artifacts meet and exchange force, motion, energy, matter or information. Interfaces carry the compatibility conditions that decide whether one design alternative can physically replace another.
data.label: Interface
data.scopeNote: Interface is reified rather than modelled as a bare relation because substitution reasoning must attach conditions, tolerances and required modifications to the junction itself.

data.definition: The motion regime in which the artifact operates.
data.label: Kinematic Condition

data.definition: A condition arising from how the artifact is made, assembled, serviced or retired.
data.label: Lifecycle Condition

data.definition: How force, moment or pressure is applied over time.
data.label: Loading Condition

data.definition: A substance, or a specified condition of a substance, from which an artifact is made, and to which property values such as strength, stiffness and hardness can be attributed.
data.label: Material
data.scopeNote: A Material instance should name its specification and condition together where the source does so (for example 'SAE 1018 low-carbon steel'), because property values are condition-dependent.

data.definition: A single characteristic of the situation in which an artifact operates: how it is loaded, how it moves, what surrounds it, how it is maintained, what it may cost.
data.label: Operating Condition

data.definition: A named bundle of operating conditions describing the situation in which an artifact must function, against which requirements, rules and substitution verdicts are evaluated.
data.label: Operating Context
data.scopeNote: An empty OperatingContext means 'context unspecified', which is not the same as 'all contexts'. Rules attached to an empty context must declare mdcore:contextUnspecified true.

data.definition: An occasional load exceeding the nominal design load, whether accidental or inherent to the duty.
data.label: Overload Condition

data.comment: Separated from Behavior so that alternatives relying on the same principle (for example every friction-based shaft/hub connection) can be retrieved as a family, independently of their geometry.
data.definition: The underlying physical principle a behavior relies on, such as dry friction, elastic deformation or contact pressure.
data.label: Physical Effect

data.definition: A numeric value together with the unit in which it was stated. Dimensionless quantities carry the explicit unit token 'dimensionless' rather than no unit at all, so that a missing unit is always an error and never an assumption.
data.label: Quantity Value
data.scopeNote: When a value has been converted, the original value and unit are retained alongside the normalized ones together with the conversion method. Conversion is never silent.

data.definition: Motion of one mating part with respect to another across a shared interface, such as axial sliding of a hub along a shaft while torque is transmitted.
data.label: Relative Motion Between Mating Parts
data.scopeNote: A decisive condition for shaft/hub connection choice, and the reason several alternatives that share the function 'transmit torque' are nonetheless not interchangeable.

data.definition: A stated condition that an acceptable design must satisfy, attributable to a stakeholder, a standard, an operating context or a physical necessity.
data.label: Requirement

data.definition: A controlled term naming the aspect of a design that a requirement addresses (load capacity, life, cost, ...).
data.label: Requirement Kind

data.definition: Cyclic loading whose direction reverses, e.g. a shaft driven in both directions.
data.label: Reversing Loading

data.definition: Position of a claim, rule or assessment on the promotion ladder.
data.label: Review State

data.definition: A qualitative degree to which an alternative meets a criterion.
data.label: Satisfaction Level

data.definition: An evaluation criterion used to choose among admissible alternatives, as opposed to one used to screen them for admissibility.
data.label: Selection Criterion

data.definition: A rule that admits, excludes or ranks alternatives for a design problem.
data.label: Selection Rule

data.definition: Load applied suddenly, with a rise time short relative to the system's response.
data.label: Shock Loading

data.definition: Load applied gradually and held essentially constant.
data.label: Static Loading

data.definition: A reified judgement about whether a candidate design alternative can take the place of a baseline design alternative, while preserving a named function, within a named operating context, under named requirements, given named modifications.
data.label: Substitution Assessment
data.scopeNote: Every assessment is directional: candidate replaces baseline. To claim the reverse, author a second assessment.

data.definition: A rule that determines the substitution state of a candidate against a baseline in a context.
data.label: Substitution Rule

data.definition: The conclusion reached by a substitution assessment.
data.label: Substitution State

data.definition: A designed artifact composed of interacting sub-artifacts that together deliver a function no single sub-artifact delivers alone, and whose boundary to its environment is explicitly identified.
data.label: Technical System

data.definition: A reified statement that some qualitative term is given a specific boundary value, valid only within a named context and only on the authority of a named source.
data.label: Threshold Definition
data.scopeNote: This class exists to prevent the ontology from asserting universal boundaries for vague terms. If no source defines a boundary, no ThresholdDefinition is created and the qualitative term remains unquantified, which downstream queries must treat as unknown rather than as false.

data.definition: A reified statement that gaining on one criterion costs performance on another, for a given alternative in a given context.
data.label: Trade-Off

data.definition: A unit of measure. Identified by a symbol string; the pipeline validates dimensional consistency with Pint rather than by OWL reasoning.
data.label: Unit

data.definition: Where a stated value came from.
data.label: Value Provenance Kind

data.definition: A defined activity that produces evidence about whether a design satisfies a requirement or resists a failure mode.
data.label: Verification Method

data.definition: A rule that determines which verification methods are required for an alternative or failure mode.
data.label: Verification Rule

properties.label: bounding box
properties.scope_note: PDF user-space coordinates as 'x0,y0,x1,y1', origin top-left, in points.

properties.definition: Links a claim to the ontology individual it concerns -- an alternative, a function, a failure mode, a verification method. This is what lets a query walk from a design object to its evidence.
properties.label: claim is about

properties.definition: Links a table, figure or equation to the span of running text that explains it, so the item is never cited stripped of the conditions its own paragraph placed on it.
properties.label: explained by surrounding text
extraction method
properties.scope_note: For example 'pymupdf-1.24.11-textdict' or 'manual-transcription-from-rendered-page'.

properties.label: local definition as given by the source

properties.definition: Fraction of characters in the span set in a mathematics font; a machine-computed proxy for text-layer risk.
properties.label: math-font character ratio
short original excerpt
properties.scope_note: Kept deliberately short; the normalized statement carries the meaning.

properties.definition: The label exactly as declared by the PDF, including non-numeric labels such as 'Cover'.
properties.label: raw page label
page label style
properties.scope_note: One of 'arabic', 'roman', 'named', 'none'.

properties.definition: Zero-based index of the page within the PDF file, as used by PyMuPDF. The canonical machine-facing locator.
properties.label: PDF page index (0-based)

properties.definition: One-based page number as shown by a PDF viewer.
properties.label: PDF page number (1-based)

properties.definition: The page number printed on the page itself, taken from the PDF page-label tree. A string, because front matter is roman and some pages carry no number.
properties.label: printed page number
properties.scope_note: MUST NOT be computed from pdfPageIndex. When absent, it is genuinely absent and the citation says so.

properties.label: symbolic expression
properties.scope_note: Transcribed by an analyst from the rendered page, not copied from the text layer, whenever ev:textIntegrity is not 'reliable'. ev:transcriptionSource records which.

properties.definition: Assessment of whether the extracted characters faithfully represent the printed glyphs.
properties.label: text-layer integrity
properties.scope_note: One of 'reliable', 'partial-glyph-loss', 'glyph-mismapped', 'unverified'. In the Shigley source, mathematics-font glyphs decode to unrelated ASCII characters, so spans covering equations are marked 'glyph-mismapped' and their text must not be quoted.

properties.label: dimension
properties.scope_note: For example '[force]', '[length]', 'dimensionless'.

properties.label: unit system required by equation
properties.scope_note: Some printed equations are dimensionally inconsistent and valid only in the units the author assumed. Recording the required system prevents silent misuse in the other system.

properties.label: analyst note
properties.scope_note: Explicitly the analyst's voice. Never quotable as source content.

properties.definition: A condition that must hold for the conclusion to apply.
properties.label: substitution condition

properties.definition: The alternative currently assumed, which the candidate would displace.
properties.label: baseline alternative

properties.definition: A condition that must hold for the behavior to occur at all, for example a maintained normal pressure for a friction-based load transfer.
properties.label: behavior requires condition

properties.definition: The alternative proposed as a replacement.
properties.label: candidate alternative

properties.definition: A quantified parameter of the condition, with its unit.
properties.label: condition parameter
condition statement
properties.scope_note: Human-readable restatement. Never the only representation: a structured condition must also be given.

properties.label: confidence
properties.scope_note: In [0,1]. An analyst's or extractor's stated confidence, never a probability derived from data unless the source supplied one.

properties.definition: Relates an interface to each artifact it joins.
properties.label: connects

properties.definition: Explicit marker that a statement's applicable context is not stated by its source. Forces the absence of context to be a recorded fact rather than an oversight.
properties.label: context deliberately unspecified
conversion method
properties.scope_note: For example 'pint 0.24; 1 psi = 6894.757 Pa; exact'. Required whenever normalizedValue differs from numericValue.

properties.definition: Relates a behavior to a structure or design alternative whose configuration makes that behavior possible.
properties.label: enabled by
evaluation numeric value
properties.scope_note: Present only when the source printed a number, or when the value is explicitly marked as an analyst-defined decision-model value via mdcore:valueProvenance.

properties.label: evaluation scale
properties.scope_note: Names the scale used, e.g. 'mdkg qualitative satisfaction scale v1' or 'lbf'.

properties.label: function being preserved
properties.scope_note: Mandatory. Substitution claims that do not say what is being preserved are not interpretable.

properties.label: has advantage
properties.scope_note: Points at an evaluation so that the advantage carries its context and provenance, rather than being a bare string.

properties.definition: Relates an artifact to a function it is intended to deliver. Intent, not observed behaviour.
properties.label: has function

properties.definition: Relates an artifact to an artifact contained within it.
properties.label: has part

properties.definition: The geometry feature at which the failure characteristically starts, such as a keyseat or a fillet.
properties.label: initiates at geometry feature

properties.definition: True when the failure of this element is deliberately preferred to the failure of adjacent, costlier components.
properties.label: is protective (sacrificial) failure
may experience failure mode
properties.scope_note: Modal by design: asserts possibility in some context, not inevitability. Pair with mdcore:aggravatedByCondition to say when.

properties.label: modification effort
properties.scope_note: Qualitative and analyst-assigned unless a source states otherwise; mark with mdcore:valueProvenance.

properties.label: ordinal rank
properties.scope_note: Ordering aid for queries. It is an ordinal, not a measurement: the gaps between ranks carry no meaning and ranks must not be averaged.

properties.definition: Relates a design alternative to a function it is capable of delivering. This is the entry point for the query 'what can perform this function?'.
properties.label: performs function
properties.scope_note: Shared performsFunction is necessary but NOT sufficient for substitutability. See mdcore:SubstitutionAssessment.

properties.definition: Relates a function to a behavior that produces it.
properties.label: realized by
rule derived from claim
properties.scope_note: Range is ev:Claim. A rule with no derived-from claim and no analyst attribution is unsupported.

properties.label: rule identifier
properties.scope_note: Must match the `id` of the corresponding entry in rules/*.yaml.

properties.definition: True when the rule expresses ontology-engineering or engineering judgement rather than a cited source statement.
properties.label: rule is analyst-authored

properties.definition: Two alternatives can perform at least one common function. Symmetric, because co-function genuinely is symmetric -- unlike substitutability, which is not.
properties.label: shares function with

properties.definition: A convenience shortcut from candidate to baseline, materialised by the build pipeline from an existing SubstitutionAssessment and never asserted by hand.
properties.label: substitution assessed as
properties.scope_note: Explicitly NOT owl:SymmetricProperty and NOT owl:TransitiveProperty. Any reasoner configuration that makes it either is a misuse of this ontology.

properties.label: test procedure specified by source
properties.scope_note: False means the source did not define instruments, load levels, cycle counts or sequence. The ontology must not supply them.

properties.label: threshold claimed universal by source
properties.scope_note: Defaults to false. Set true only when the source explicitly presents the boundary as generally valid.

properties.label: threshold scope note
properties.scope_note: Records the limits the source itself placed on the boundary, e.g. that no sharp dividing line exists.

properties.label: unit symbol
properties.scope_note: Use 'dimensionless' for pure numbers such as a design factor.

properties.label: uses equation
properties.scope_note: Range is ev:Equation, declared in the evidence module.

properties.label: value provenance
properties.scope_note: Required on every AlternativeEvaluation and on every numeric value that is not directly quoted from a source.

properties.definition: Relates an alternative, requirement or failure mode to a method that checks it.
properties.label: verified by
designation system
properties.scope_note: For example 'SAE', 'UNS', 'AISI', 'ASTM', 'ISO'.

properties.definition: True when the element is normally bought to a published standard rather than made to a drawing.
properties.label: is a standard catalogue item
material designation
properties.scope_note: The designation exactly as printed by the source, e.g. 'SAE 1018'. Designation systems differ; do not translate silently.

properties.definition: True when the connection can be taken apart and reassembled with ordinary maintenance tooling.
properties.label: permits field disassembly

properties.definition: Relates a design alternative to a process its realisation demands. Central to substitution: an alternative that requires a process the shop does not have is not available regardless of its performance.
properties.label: requires manufacturing process
stress concentration factor
properties.scope_note: Dimensionless, and always tied to a loading mode and a geometry ratio. A factor cited without its loading mode is uninterpretable and must not be stored.

properties.label: loading mode for stress concentration factor
properties.scope_note: For example 'bending', 'torsion', 'axial'.

properties.label: values are typical, not guaranteed
properties.scope_note: Set true when the source labels its table as typical. This is a real constraint on how the value may be used in design, and it is lost if only the number is stored.

properties.label: uses element type
properties.scope_note: Range is a punned element-type individual. Punning is used rather than a parallel individual hierarchy so that the taxonomy is not duplicated.
